newsitem.title: USA: Attorney for family calls Simpson "vengeful killer".
newsitem.headline: Attorney for family calls Simpson "vengeful killer".

text.p: Opening arguments began on Wednesday in the O.J. Simpson civil trial with an attorney branding the former football star a "vengeful killer" and vowing to prove that he committed a brutal double-murder.

In an impassioned presentation, Daniel Petrocelli, a lawyer for the family of murder victim Ronald Goldman, told jurors Goldman "died with his eyes open" and the last thing he saw was the man who killed him and his friend, Nicole Brown Simpson, O.J. Simpson's ex-wife.
"We will prove to you that Ronald Goldman and Nicole Brown Simpson died at the hands of the defendant, Orenthal James Simpson," Petrocelli told jurors.
"We will prove to you Ron and Nicole were killed quickly and savagely," he said. "They were defenceless against a man who was large, strong, armed with a 6-in (15-cm) knife and in a state of rage."
Simpson, who was acquitted of murder on Oct. 3, 1995, after a year-long trial, is now in civil court facing a wrongful-death lawsuit brought by the victims' families.
Clad in a gray suit, Simpson sat just behind the defence table, sometimes shaking his head as Petrocelli spoke.
Simpson's lawyers are expected in their opening statement to use many of the same claims of police frameup and evidence of contamination that won an acquittal in the criminal trial.
The courtroom was packed for Wednesday's session. Members of the mostly white jury -- a reversal in the racial makeup of the criminal trial's mostly black panel -- listened intently.
Simpson's elderly mother, Eunice, looked on from her wheelchair. Some of the victims' relatives sat sobbing in the spectators' gallery.

In a stinging opening statement, Petrocelli alleged that Simpson killed Goldman on June 12, 1994, to eliminate a witness to the fatal attack on Simpson's ex-wife, only moments before, outside her townhouse. He portrayed Goldman as a hero who stayed to face down the murderer.
Petrocelli said Goldman was doing a favour for his friend -- returning a pair of glasses from the restaurant where he worked as a waiter -- "only to come upon her vengeful killer."
"In the last furious moments of his life, Ron Goldman saw through his eyes the man who killed his friend Nicole and took his young life away, the man who sits in this courtroom," he said.
Petrocelli promised to present evidence that jurors in the criminal trial never heard about -- Simpson's statement to police and the freeway chase that led to his arrest.

He also said he would introduce a photograph showing that Simpson lied during his pre-trial deposition when he denied owning a pair of Bruno Magli shoes, saying, "I would have never owned those ugly-assed shoes."

And he said one of the nation's leading pathologists, Werner Spitz, who helped to investigate the assassinations of John F. Kennedy and Martin Luther King Jr., would testify that the cuts on Simpson's hand were gouges caused by the fingernails of one of the victims.

In terms of its racial breakdown, the jury bears little resemblance to the panel that acquitted Simpson in his criminal trial. It is made up of seven women and five men, among them eight whites, one black, one Hispanic, one person of Hispanic and white descent and one Asian-black.
Superior Court Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki has banned cameras and microphones, blacking out the proceedings to millions of TV viewers who followed the first trial.

Dozens of camera crews swarmed the lawn outside the Santa Monica courthouse on Wednesday, and a handful of demonstrators and publicity seekers turned out. But it was far more subdued scene than the media frenzy that surrounded the first trial.

Simpson never took the witness stand during the last trial but he will be forced to testify in civil court. He cannot be punished with jail but he could be forced to pay millions in damages if found "liable" for the murders.

Unlike the criminal trial, which required "proof beyond a reasonable doubt," the plaintiffs in the civil trial will prevail if they can prove there is a 50.1 percent probability -- a "preponderance of the evidence" -- that Simpson committed the murders. And only nine of the 12 jurors' votes are required for a judgment for or against Simpson. The trial is expected to last at about four months.
